modelingNotes: Ally Charlotte Center (601 S Tryon St, 2021, Crescent Communities; Gensler), Charlotte — original procedural geometry, CC0-1.0. bun generators/clt-ally-center.ts

Map frame: x east, y north, z up, metres; origin at the anchor (the centroid of the OSM outline way/1046738978) on the lowest ground. Placed at bearing 49.2, square to Uptown's grid: -x faces South Tryon Street (north-west), +y faces Stonewall Street (north-east).

Identity, in order: - a plain 26-storey slab, long side on Tryon, under a white screen crown carrying the magenta "ally" sign at its Tryon face's south-west end; - its two facets: most of the tower is a grey aluminium grid, one cell to two storeys, while the north corner (Tryon and Stonewall) is a sheer flush glass block standing a little proud of the grid; - the tall glazed lobby on Tryon and the low brick retail podium at each end.

Evidence: - OSM: outline way/1046738978 (tagged 130 m, 26 levels, Q48840112), parts way/1351695576 (the tower, 110 m: a 40 x 75 m rectangle), way/1351695577 and way/1351695578 (7 m retail at the north-east and south-west ends), way/1351695582-585 (rooftop plant, 117-123 m, inside the screen). Plan measured from these. - Published: 378 ft / 115.2 m, 26 floors, completed 2021 (CTBUH, via Wikipedia "Ally Charlotte Center" and "List of tallest buildings in Charlotte"). The 115.2 m is taken as the screen's top; OSM's 130 m on the outline matches no photo and is not used. - Lidar: USGS_LPC_NC_Phase4_Mecklenburg_2016 (flown 2016-17) predates the tower (the site was a surface lot); not used for heights. - Photos (Wikimedia Commons, daylight): "Ally Charlotte Center.jpg" (Jt12081988, CC BY-SA 4.0, elevated, from across Tryon: the grid, the flush corner block, the screen and sign, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ally_Charlotte_Center.jpg); "Ally Charlotte Center S Tryon St.jpg" (City Dweller 2, CC BY-SA 4.0, the Tryon face and lobby, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ally_Charlotte_Center_S_Tryon_St.jpg); "Ally Center Charlotte May 2022.jpg" (City Dweller 2, CC BY-SA 4.0, from Tryon to the north-east, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ally_Center_Charlotte_May_2022.jpg); "Ally building 2019.jpg" (Cmett003, CC BY-SA 4.0, under construction: the two facets meeting, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ally_building_2019.jpg); "Ally Charlotte Center Restaurants Along South Tryon Late March 2024.jpg" and "Ally Charlotte Center Dos Caminos Late March 2024.jpg" (City Dweller 2, CC BY-SA 4.0, the brick podium, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ally_Charlotte_Center_Restaurants_Along_South_Tryon_Late_March_2024.jpg, https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Ally_Charlotte_Center_Dos_Caminos_Late_March_2024.jpg). Mapillary was searched; its nearby images show only the street. No commercial imagery. No look-only sources were used.

Estimated: the roof at 109 m and the screen 109-115.2 m (one and a half storeys in the photos); the lobby 13 m (three storeys); the grid's cells, 8 m (two storeys) by ~7 m (seven cells and the flush block on Tryon, per Jt12081988's photo); the flush block's extent (22 m along Tryon, 16 m along Stonewall) and its 0.8 m projection, read off the photos; the podium's brick, a buff between the red and the tan brick the photos show. The "ally" sign is drawn as plain block letters: it is the one mark that names the tower from the street and the skyline.

Doubts: the south-east (back) and south-west faces are unphotographed and are drawn as grid like the Tryon face; the flush block's return along Stonewall is seen only obliquely. OSM's 123 m plant box is not drawn, as nothing shows above the screen. Left out: mullions, the floor lines in the flush glass, the Tryon canopy, the plaza and the JW Marriott next door.

Original procedural model from https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks (catalog id "clt-ally-center", model "clt-ally-center"), generated by https://github.com/alexwohlbruck/landmarks/blob/a1974bbf738c6994edbe99a7a61818b9d69da9e0/generators/clt-ally-center.ts. That repository is the editable source; source.blend.gz is the exported mesh imported into Blender for convenience.

Exported for Open Landmarks v1: placement bearing and scale baked in; moving parts frozen in their rest pose; footings and basements below the lowest ground (y = 0) cut away; material colours carried over exactly, as library finishes where they are not standard swatches.
